resources: Mobility Lens Assignment 1 Mobility Lens Android application that helps a developer consider the design implications of six dimensions Input and interaction Mobile apps mainly use touch, gestures, and on-screen keyboards Buttons and controls should be easy to tap and simple to use Screen size, orientation, and density Phones come in many screen sizes and can switch between portrait and landscape Developers should make layouts flexible so they work well on different devices Lifecycle and resource constraints Mobile devices have limited battery, memory, and processing power, and apps may be paused in the background Apps should save user progress and avoid using unnecessary resources Context awareness Phones can use things like location, camera, Bluetooth, and sensors Developers can use these features but must handle permissions and battery usage carefully Usage patterns Mobile apps are often used for short periods and users may be interrupted frequently Tasks should be quick, simple, and easy to continue later Security and privacy expectations Phones often contain sensitive personal information Developers should protect user data and only request permissions that are actually needed Previous" Next" Submit Error: Text field cannot be empty %1$s must account for %2$s Dimension %1$d of %2$d The constraint What it means for your app Check your own work Application or feature name Offline receipt scanner
